objectives: Recognize common CVC word families in controlled w-reading.
Blend and read w-initial CVC words accurately.
Compare onsets and rimes in simple CVC words.
Read controlled phrases and sentences with increasing fluency.
concepts: A word family shares the same rime.
Changing the onset can create another word in the same family.

definitions.definition: A group of words that share the same ending sound and spelling pattern.
The initial consonant sound or consonant group before the rime in a syllable.
The vowel and sounds that follow the onset in a syllable.
Reading text built mainly from phonics patterns that have been explicitly taught.

workedExamples: wag → tag: onset changes, -ag stays the same.
wet → jet: onset changes, -et stays the same.
wig → big: onset changes, -ig stays the same.
commonMistakes: Treating the whole word as one memorized unit.
Changing the rime when only the onset should change.
Guessing a word from its first letter.
Skipping a word instead of blending and rereading.

basic: Sort simple CVC words by shared rime.
conceptual: Identify whether two CVC words share a word family.
application: Read controlled w-CVC phrases and sentences.
higherOrderThinking: Explain how changing the onset changes a word while preserving the rime.
mixedReview: Mix word-family recognition, decoding and controlled reading.

quickRevision: find the rime → blend the onset → read the word → reread the sentence
mistakeBasedRevision: If a word is guessed, return to the letters, segment the sounds and blend again.
weakTopicRevision: Practise the specific rime that is not yet automatic.

activities.name: Word-family sort
steps: Group words with the same rime.

activities.name: Controlled reread
steps: Check that every word was decoded.

outcomes: Learner identifies shared rimes in taught CVC words.
Learner reads w-initial CVC words accurately.
Learner reads controlled sentences with improved accuracy and fluency.
